artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan (2.5h) repairing the stale cycle_plan_dispatch_hash() strip pattern that keeps the IDENTICAL DISPATCH HALT inert, with a red-first Group 27 regression fixture, separate landing of the orphaned H1 fix, known-failures.txt row deletion, and redeploy.

memory_candidates.content: Cross-script content-hashing contracts have a silent staleness failure mode: when script A computes a digest over content script B generates, and A strips a known-varying line set before hashing, any later addition of per-invocation-varying content to B's template silently invalidates A's normalization -- and neither script's own tests catch it, because B's tests only check B's output and A's tests use hand-written fixtures frozen at A's authoring time. The symptom is a guard that goes inert rather than failing loudly: every downstream back-out step of the guard appears broken at once, which looks like many bugs but is one upstream predicate never satisfied. Two structural fixes together, not either alone: (1) a forward-pointer comment in the GENERATING script at each varying interpolation site, pointing at the normalizer's strip pattern, so the next editor is warned in the file they are actually editing; (2) an isolated unit-level fixture over the normalizer that enumerates ALL known varying locations, so a new one fails a cheap test rather than silently degrading an expensive live-pipeline guard. A comment in the normalizer alone listing what it strips is insufficient -- nobody editing the generator reads it.
